I farm the same 7 mu in wheat-maize rotation, so I do not start from zero. I look at what worked last year, what the neighbors around Quzhou County are doing, and what I can afford. With 7 mu and well water, I will not be stingy on fertilizer, because if wheat or maize goes hungry, the yield loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also will not throw money around. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough base fertilizer in the ground, and give it about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu over the season. I will water about 3 times if the year is normal: once before winter if the ground is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I usually spray 2 times, mainly for weeds and then disease or aphids if they show. I will use rotary tillage for wheat because the straw and seedbed are easier that way on my land. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because around here the hybrids usually stand better and yield better if water keeps up. I will put about 20 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu on maize. Maize eats fertilizer hard, so I would rather feed it enough. I will water 2 times in a normal year, around big flare-up growth and silking or grain filling, depending on rain. I usually spray 2 times for weeds and then insects or leaf disease if needed. For maize after wheat, I can keep tillage lighter, so I will do rotary tillage and sow quickly after harvest. If weather is normal and I manage on time, I will aim around 500 kg per mu for wheat and 600 kg per mu for maize.
